key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity lowers their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters and accounting for service humidity can help tailor protective coatings for Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings by detonation spray under varied spraying parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating porosity, and lamellar microstructure.
Evaluate corrosion behavior and sliding wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance gains or humidity ranges, and the wear findings involve a specific Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
